Subject: Private offer ask — dual-listing and reseller margin

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this. ProspectCo is asking us to run a private offer on AWS (they prefer private-offer flow) but they also need dual-list pricing: marketplace list for procurement + a direct invoice route for their finance team (they have an internal vendor policy). They want a clear channel margin waterfall so our reseller can price their services on top.

Quick asks:
- Can Redwood support a private-offer where the SKU remains listed but settlement occurs via a direct invoice?
- What's the standard channel margin waterfall you recommend for a reseller-managed private offer (we need to propose an initial % to ProspectCo before their CFO signs off)?
- Any constraints around overages/true-ups for metered SKUs and invoice routing?

We attached our partner template and a simple margin model. Happy to jump on a 30-min call this week.

Attachments: reseller_template.pdf (partner template), initial_margin_model.xlsx (calc)

Best,
Alex Ramos

Subject: Re: Private offer ask — dual-listing and reseller margin

Alex — thanks for the clear summary. Short answers up front: yes, we can support a dual-listing/settlement pattern but there are a few guardrails that matter for billing and margin calculations. Ben and Jordan are looped in to finalize the channel split and invoice flow.

We need clarity on two things before we propose a firm % to ProspectCo:
1) Commit corridor: will ProspectCo commit to a minimum monthly USD usage for the private-offer SKU, or do they want fully metered? Commit materially changes the margin waterfall.
2) Invoice destination: when you say "direct invoice route" — do you mean Redwood invoices via the reseller (pass-through) or Redwood invoices ProspectCo directly while the reseller retains a commission?

What I can propose now:
- Preliminary margin offer to the reseller: 14% net on list price for pure metered (no commit).
- If ProspectCo signs a 12-month commit with a 20% volume corridor, we can improve reseller net to 18% and allow a small up-front implementation credit.

Next steps: Ben to validate tax/invoice routing and Jordan to draft the private-offer doc for AWS/GCP flow (including required contract language to allow pass-through invoicing). If you can send the negotiated commitment level, I will share a draft PO and a margin workbook.

Irene Choi
Head of Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com

From: ben.carter@redwood.com

Date: Fri, 13 Apr 2028 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: internal: suggested waterfall + invoice routing (for Alex)

Irene / Jordan — looping on Alex's ask. High-level suggestions we can send externally once aligned:

Proposed waterfall (examples):
- List price (Marketplace SKU) = $1.00 per unit
  - Reseller gross margin: 25% of list (competitive starter)
  - Redwood net after reseller: 75% of list
  - Platform/marketplace fees (AWS/GCP marketplace fee) deducted prior to Redwood settlement ~7%
  - Effective Redwood revenue = 0.75 * (1 - 0.07) = 0.6975 -> our baseline 

Compact offer options:
- Metered, no commit: Reseller net 14% of list (as Irene suggested) — suitable for trials
- 12-mo commit (>= monthly USD floor): Reseller net 18% + $X implementation credit (amortized)
- True-up model: monthly true-up based on ingestion; true-up invoices routed to reseller; we require monthly usage export to reconcile.

Invoice routing notes:
- Preferred: Reseller invoices ProspectCo (pass-through), Redwood invoices reseller. This preserves reseller accounting but requires reseller to accept marketplace terms for reconciliation.
- Alternate: Redwood invoices ProspectCo directly and pays reseller commission. This is simpler for reconciliation on our side but ProspectCo finance must accept Redwood as vendor (the ask earlier).

I'll finalize the spreadsheet with two scenarios (metered/no-commit vs commit corridor) and include a lane for marketplace fee layering and tax handling.

Ben Carter
Channel Finance Lead | Redwood Inference

Alex / Mark (ProspectCo) — thanks for the patience. Attached are two items: a draft Private Offer PDF that reflects the dual-listing wording we discussed and an editable channel-margin workbook (channel-margin-model.xlsx) showing the scenarios below.

Summary proposal (sendable to ProspectCo CFO):
- Dual-listing construct: SKU remains visible in AWS Marketplace for procurement records; settlement elected as "reseller pass-through" where Redwood invoices the reseller and the reseller invoices ProspectCo.
- Metered / no commitment: Reseller commission 14% of Marketplace list. Marketplace fee (~7%) and taxes are excluded from the reseller commission calculation.
- 12-month commit corridor: If ProspectCo commits to >= $120k ARR equivalent (monthly smoothing allowed), reseller commission increases to 18% and Redwood provides a $10k implementation credit (amortized across invoices).
- True-up: Monthly usage true-up; reseller receives monthly settlement statements; Redwood will publish a CSV usage export within 3 business days of month close for reconciliation.
- Invoice routing: Redwood -> Reseller -> ProspectCo (pass-through) preferred. If ProspectCo requires Redwood direct invoicing, we will convert to a commission-with-payment model and provide a separate commission statement cadence.

Next steps:
1) Alex / ResellerCo: confirm whether ProspectCo is willing to sign a 12-month commit or prefers metered.
2) If commit, sign the attached Private_Offer_Draft_v2.pdf and return to us; we will then issue a DocuSign envelope (link included) for Redwood signatures.
3) Ben will drop final numbers into channel-margin-model.xlsx and send an invoice routing checklist.

Docs attached: Private_Offer_Draft_v2.pdf (draft PO), channel-margin-model.xlsx (scenario workbook)

If helpful, Ben and I are available for a 30-min technical-commercial sync Monday.

Irene Choi
